6 الطَّيْرُ تَتَنَاوَحُ [The birds warble plaintively, one to another]. (A.) See an ?? in art. فوح, conj. 6. ―
-b2- تناوحتِ الرِّيَاحُ The winds blew violently [as is generally the case when they blow from opposite directions]. (TA.) See an ex. voce سهو. ―
-b3- تناوحا They two were opposite, one to the other; they faced each other. (S, K.) You say so of two mountains, and of two winds. (S, L.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
